authority_basis.claim_scope: Scalar/vector distinction, vector magnitude, direction and notation.

concepts.statement: A vector requires magnitude and spatial direction and obeys vector addition; a scalar does not.
concepts.why_required: This distinguishes physical vectors from scalars before any vector algebra is attempted.
concepts.failure_if_omitted: Directional wording may be mistaken for vector structure and later addition rules become incoherent.

concepts.statement: Vector direction is meaningful only relative to a declared axis, bearing convention, or equivalent reference.
concepts.why_required: Signs and angles cannot be interpreted without a declared directional reference.
concepts.failure_if_omitted: The same vector description can be assigned incompatible signs or angles.

model_conditions.condition: Vector is represented in a Euclidean spatial model.
model_conditions.physical_reason: The ordinary magnitude and directed-segment interpretation assume Euclidean geometry.
model_conditions.failure_consequence: A different mathematical vector space may require a different norm or interpretation.

representations.semantic_geometry: A directed segment encodes a start point, direction and length proportional to magnitude relative to a declared reference.
must_not_imply: the drawing scale itself proves the numerical magnitude
directional wording alone makes a quantity a vector
representations.verification_method: Check arrow direction against the declared reference and keep magnitude nonnegative.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Classify the physical quantity as scalar or vector.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: Scalar and vector operations may be mixed without justification.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Declare the direction reference before interpreting sign or angle.
Separate the vector symbol from its nonnegative scalar magnitude.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: Signed components may be confused with vector magnitude.

required_transformations.description: Map a directed physical quantity to a vector symbol while keeping its magnitude as a separate nonnegative scalar.
Use the declared direction reference to interpret the vector consistently inside a problem.

misconceptions.incorrect_model: Any quantity described with a direction is automatically a vector.
misconceptions.why_plausible: Everyday language uses direction loosely and can hide whether the quantity obeys vector addition.
misconceptions.required_counterexample: A scalar speed can be reported while motion direction is separately described; the scalar itself still does not obey vector addition.
misconceptions.required_representation_repair: Contrast a scalar label with a directed arrow that has a declared reference.
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Require vector addition behaviour and spatial transformation, not directional wording alone.
misconceptions.verification: Test whether the quantity combines according to vector addition.

problem_families.name: Identify scalar versus vector quantities
problem_families.first_technical_move: Identify whether vector addition and spatial direction are intrinsic to the quantity.
fatal_errors: treating directional wording as sufficient proof of vector character

problem_families.name: Specify vector magnitude and direction
problem_families.first_technical_move: Declare the direction reference before interpreting the angle.
fatal_errors: using an angle without a reference axis

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Remove the direction-reference invariant from vector basics.
